title: Do LLMs Have Values? A Quantitative Analysis and Alignment Framework for Values in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.16589v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly handle complex subjective tasks, aligning their intentions and behaviors with human values has become a critical scientific challenge. However, current efforts are confounded by a striking behavioral paradox: they fluctuate unpredictably under minor wording changes ("swing"), yet stubbornly ignore explicit instructions to correct ingrained biases ("rigidity"). Resolving this duality is critical for reliable AI alignment. To systematically understand and safely steer these latent subjective preferences, our study is structured around three fundamental questions. First, do LLMs possess an intrinsic value system? By projecting responses from 106 LLMs (150,000 queries per model) and 95,000 human survey profiles into a shared sociological space, we empirically confirm that they do. However, they do not mirror human diversity, instead crystallizing into a highly concentrated, idealized value core. S

translated_title: 大语言模型有价值观吗？大语言模型价值观的定量分析与对齐框架
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地处理复杂的主观任务，将其意图和行为与人类价值观对齐已成为一个关键的科学挑战。然而，目前的努力被一个显著的行为悖论所困扰：它们在微小的措辞变化下会不可预测地波动（“摇摆”），却又顽固地无视纠正根深蒂固偏见的明确指令（“僵化”）。解决这种双重性对于可靠的AI对齐至关重要。为了系统地理解并安全地引导这些潜在的主观偏好，我们的研究围绕三个基本问题展开。首先，大语言模型是否拥有内在的价值体系？通过将106个大语言模型（每个模型150,000次查询）的响应和95,000份人类调查档案投射到一个共享的社会学空间中，我们实证证实了它们确实拥有。然而，它们并不反映人类的多样性，而是结晶成一个高度集中的、理想化的价值观核心。
tldr: 本研究通过将106个大语言模型与95,000份人类调查档案投射到共享的社会学空间进行大规模定量分析，实证证实了LLMs拥有内在但高度集中、理想化的价值观体系，并提出了应对其“摇摆”与“僵化”双重行为悖论的对齐框架。
en_tdlr: Through large-scale quantitative analysis projecting 106 LLMs and 95,000 human survey profiles into a shared sociological space, this study empirically confirms that LLMs possess an intrinsic yet highly concentrated and idealized value system, and proposes an alignment framework to address the dual "swing-rigidity" behavioral paradox.
